brief.subject: Robinson nuclear verdict upheld; California diesel stays above $8
brief.headline: Texas Judge Upholds C.H. Robinson Nuclear Verdict; California Diesel Holds Above $8
brief.dek: A major broker verdict stands, California fuel stays painful, cargo crime cases hit trucking, and intermodal and port volumes run hot.
brief.lede: A Texas judge has affirmed the nuclear verdict against C.H. Robinson. That keeps liability risk front and center for anyone moving freight through brokers.

sections.heading: Robinson Nuclear Verdict Stands
bullets: A Texas judge affirmed the nuclear verdict against C.H. Robinson, one of the largest freight brokers.
Large jury awards remain a live threat across the supply chain, so watch for knock-on effects on insurance and carrier vetting.

sections.heading: California Diesel Stuck Above $8
bullets: Above $8 per gallon: California diesel stays elevated as truckers push for relief.
An energy expert warns high costs could last well into next year, so price fuel into every West Coast lane.
Big shippers are hedging and using route optimization to absorb diesel costs, so expect pushback on fuel surcharges.

sections.heading: Crime Cases Target Trucking
bullets: 25 charged: a drug ring used unsuspecting trucking companies to move cocaine from California to Florida.
More than 45 kilograms of cocaine seized; know your shippers and inspect loads that seem off.
32 months: Louisiana staged-accident mastermind Danny Keating was sentenced in a case tied to fraud against truckers.

sections.heading: Volumes Run Hot at Rail and Ports
bullets: 10%: intermodal rail volumes kept a strong pace in the latest U.S. traffic count, competing for long-haul freight.
Near 1M containers: Port of Long Beach set an all-time monthly record in September, feeding drayage and outbound loads.
J.B. Hunt reported Q3 growing pains and cost pressures, though management called it a speed bump toward recovery.
